@graph.name: Do we need a Sana Commerce alternative for spoken orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Sana Commerce carries on with its online work, from account pricing to web orders. Our app is for each chef still calling: they read each item into it, look the list over, and what was a call reaches you already checked.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Sana Commerce?

acceptedAnswer.text: At one thing: the order from a chef who likes saying it more than logging in to shop. Sana covers far more, from quotes and payments to returns, so we run alongside it and are not a Sana Commerce alternative.

@graph.name: Does Sana Commerce have its own app or voice ordering?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not that we found. Its store is built to work in a phone's browser. The older Sana mobile app in its help pages was made for sales agents, and we did not find it on the current site. We searched for voice or phone-order tools built for Sana and came up empty. Ours is an app on the chef's own phone.

@graph.name: Will my desk still type these orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on how they reach you. Our app and your web store come from different companies, each supporting only its own software. Through EDI or the API, our order can go into your ERP with no retyping if your system takes orders that way, and the demo will show whether it does. By email, it arrives as an attached file, and your desk enters it from that. What your desk saves is the call: no order to take down, write out and read back, just a list the chef looked over before sending. Looking it over does not rule out mistakes, since speech becomes items from the guide and a chef can miss a wrong one or change their mind after sending. Your ERP stays the record for customers, stock and invoices; we hold each restaurant's order guide, with the prices you set, plus the orders sent through the app. A phone call still gets no order number from us.

@graph.name: Will an app order show up in Sana?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not as a web order, because it never passes through the Sana store. Once your ERP has it, it is an ERP order, the same as one your team took by phone, and Sana can still list it on that customer's account, since Sana shows ERP orders there too.

@graph.name: Sana already cut our price and stock calls. Which calls are left?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, the order calls themselves. Sana goes after routine reorders too, with order templates, reorders of earlier purchases and subscriptions, for customers signed in to the store. Any calls still coming from chefs who would rather read out a list than open a store are the ones we built the app around.

@graph.name: When could we start, and what does it cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Setup is 24 to 48 hours for most distributors, with Sana and your ERP left untouched. You send what each account regularly orders, often exported from your ERP. We load those items into our admin, set up each account, and the restaurants get the app on their phones; most send in a first order that same day. Sana publishes two timelines for building its own store, three or six months with someone from your team on the project. Sana asks you to request pricing for each plan, and we quote per distributor as well. A Sana Commerce replacement would put a new store in front of web customers already happy on Sana, which is not what we offer.
